title: How he developed his high notes
summary: He explains going above the staff, copying Armstrong's 'Shine', and going up to F above high C.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Can you tell us a little bit about the way that you were playing at this time because your emphasis was very much on, you know, the upper end registar. You know, the high notes and things like that. And, this was one thing that you did extremely well.
Can you tell us something about your interest in high notes and how that happened

I suppose I can say it this way. Well, like I said, it was from my first teacher. And then I started playing the same tune. When I heard somebody playing a tune just right on the staff, I just tried something different. In other words, I just went above that. I said I wanted to try this, play this at another staff just often higher.

And I went that way, and it kept coming to me that way. And when I heard Louis do the "Shine" and do these high C's on that end, then I copied that. I liked it so well and then while he was making 30 and 40, I went on until I went up to 100. I said, I just kept counting — the boys were counting behind me — (inaudible), and then I went from there to F which is above high C. And from then on, when I started having an arrangement made, then they started writing it up there for me. They started writing the high notes from the beginning. I used to

play an F like up in front of the band. My trumpet section was playing and I used to take all the top parts. If they just played the regular, whatever is on the sheet, I used to go for the top. Then, I had the notes going above C. I used to do that.

I remember playing "Shine" in the theater and the people applauded me back. I was tired. What would I do? I'd take "Stardust" and play a chorus of "Stardust". When I got around to the end of it, what did I do? I played above and ended on a fortissimo B flat. You know, after doing all that.
It didn't come to me too hard cause I was used to it. I was even doing it through my younger days.
You know, like I said, my first teacher who was called "High C" Foster. It came to me a little easy.
